verdict.rationale: Rootly documents alert deduplication in depth: repeat events from the same monitor collapse onto a single open alert via a stable identifier, so responders see a climbing count instead of being re-paged. Grouping of related, non-identical alerts appears only as one summary line on the alerts overview, with no documented grouping rules or behavior, so that half of the story is thin. missing for 10: documented related-alert grouping mechanics (rules, time windows, cross-source correlation), evidence that grouped alerts produce a single page, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, duplicate and related alerts are deduplicated and grouped so one incident pages one human, not fifty

citations.quote: Collapse repeat events from the same monitor into a single open Rootly alert using a stable identifier, so responders aren't paged twice.
Alert Deduplication collapses those repeat events onto a single open alert, so the responder sees the count climbing instead of getting paged again.
Rootly deduplicates repeats, groups related alerts together, routes each one to the right team
